boundary_rationale: The title is one counted MT verse (web:Ps.62.0 = oshb:Ps.62.1), naming the Jeduthun setting (one of 3 Ps psalms so labeled, with Psalms 39 and 77). The unit is a ring: it opens on (oshb:Ps.62.2) אַ֣ךְ אֶל אֱ֭לֹהִים דּֽוּמִיָּ֣ה “My soul rests in God alone” (web:Ps.62.1), turns at web:Ps.62.3 to a complaint against attackers, “How long will you assault a man?”, and returns to the same confidence idiom at (oshb:Ps.62.6) אַ֣ךְ לֵ֭אלֹהִים דּ֣וֹמִּי נַפְשִׁ֑י “My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.” (web:Ps.62.5), completing the envelope. Collated against oshb:Ps.62.6, oshb:Ps.62.2 shares no tier — real lexical substitution: (oshb:Ps.62.2) אֶל אֱ֭לֹהִים against (oshb:Ps.62.6) לֵ֭אלֹהִים, and (oshb:Ps.62.2) יְשׁוּעָתִֽי against (oshb:Ps.62.6) תִּקְוָתִֽי — so the return is thematic anaphora (sweep: 6 verses open with אך in Ps 62, 34 verses / 36 token-occurrences book-wide at skeleton tier), not a repeated line.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the ring at its individual אך-openings into separate one- or two-verse rows was rejected, since the confidence-complaint-confidence pattern needs the full envelope to complete, not one opening on its own.
observed_substrate_signals: אך opens (oshb:Ps.62.2) אַ֣ךְ, oshb:Ps.62.3, and (oshb:Ps.62.5) אַ֤ךְ inside this row, plus 2 more later in the psalm: 6 verse-initial occurrences of אך among Ps 62’s 12 MT body verses; a separate contiguous-consonantal-substring sweep finds 34 verses (36 token-occurrences) book-wide at skeleton tier.

oshb:Ps.62.3 opens with אַךְ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י, echoed at this row’s own closing verse, oshb:Ps.62.7 (=web:Ps.62.6), whose opening five tokens repeat oshb:Ps.62.3 byte-for-byte; beyond those five tokens, oshb:Ps.62.7’s own tokens 6-7 are skeleton-identical to oshb:Ps.62.3’s, differing only in accents, and oshb:Ps.62.3 carries one further token, רַבָּֽה, which oshb:Ps.62.7 lacks.
Selah closes web:Ps.62.4 (oshb:Ps.62.5), mid-ring rather than at the row’s own end — disclosed, not treated as the driver.
